paper_sections.title: Neural Correlates of Social Inclusion in Borderline Personality Disorder
Interaction effect of group and ball tossing condition

description.value: The study examined neural correlates of social inclusion and exclusion in females with borderline personality disorder, major depressive disorder, and healthy controls using the Cyberball fMRI paradigm, and related brain responses to psychopathological features.

design.value: A cross-sectional between-group fMRI study using a within-subject three-condition Cyberball paradigm and second-level group-by-condition analyses.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID-I and -II)

description.value: Used to verify clinical diagnoses of major depression and borderline personality disorder.
Assessed BPD symptom severity; total scores were divided by the number of items.
Assessed current depressive symptoms in its German version.
A 30-item self-report questionnaire measuring impulsivity, with each item rated on a 4-point Likert scale.

Assessed rejection sensitivity, defined as anxious expectation, ready perception and overreaction to rejection cues; total scores were calculated from anxiety or concern and inverted expectancy of acceptance scores.
An eight-question scale examining sensitivity in social situations, with each question rated on a 5-point Likert scale.
A 20-item scale assessing distress after social exclusion across feeling excluded, low self-worth, meaningless existence, and control.

name.value: Feelings after fMRI visual rating scale

description.value: Participants rated angry, sad, happy, afraid, frustrated, satisfied, helpless, and inner tension from 1 (very low) to 4 (very strong) after the entire fMRI-Cyberball paradigm.

source_definition.value: Participants aged 18–40 years; age was included as a covariate because MD patients were significantly older than BPD patients and HC.
Scanner type was included as a covariate because BPD and HC data were acquired on a different scanner than MD data.

description.value: Seventeen healthy controls served as control group with no current or lifetime psychiatric diagnoses.

medical_condition.value: no current or lifetime psychiatric diagnoses

recruitment_method.value: inpatient and outpatient units of the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy of the University Hospital Ulm

description.value: Fifteen patients diagnosed with BPD; 13 had comorbid major depression, two had remitted depression, eight met criteria for PTSD and two met criteria for dysthymia according DSM-IV.

medical_condition.value: major depression, posttraumatic stress disorder, dysthymia

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID-I and -II)

clinical_characteristics.value: Thirteen of the 15 BPD-patients had a comorbid MD, two BPD-subjects were diagnosed with a remitted depression. Eight patients of the BPD-group met also criteria of PTSD and 2 met criteria of dysthymia according DSM-IV.

medication_status.value: Twelve patients of the BPD-group took antidepressants and one was medicated with lithium.

recruitment_method.value: inpatient and outpatient units of the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy of the University Hospital Ulm

description.value: Sixteen patients diagnosed with major depressive disorder; two met criteria for dysthymia and one had a history of remitted anorexia.

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID-I and -II)

clinical_characteristics.value: In the MD-group, two subjects met criteria of dysthymia according DSM-IV but had no other psychiatric diagnoses at the time of investigation and one had a history of remitted anorexia.

medication_status.value: All MD-patients took antidepressant medication of various kinds; one had concomitant medication with topiramate, one with quetiapine and one with pregabalin. Sedative drugs were disrupted prior to scanning.

recruitment_method.value: inpatient and outpatient units of the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy of the University Hospital Ulm

task_description.value: Participants took part in a virtual ball-tossing game with two other supposed participants. They were represented by a hand and the other players by animated comic figures; in fact, participants played against the computer and all actions were pre-programmed.

design_type.value: three different conditions, each applied once, each lasting around 2 min

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to take part in the virtual ball-tossing game. During passive watching, participants were asked just to watch the game and the computer controlled their character.

stimuli.value: Virtual ball-tossing game with two animated comic figures; each condition involved 60 throws.

task_performance_measures.value: Subjective emotional experience regarding angry, sad, happy, afraid, frustrated, satisfied, helpless, and inner tension, rated after fMRI on a visual rating scale from 1 (very low) to 4 (very strong).

description.value: T2*-sensitive gradient echo sequence for functional imaging during the Cyberball task; 35 transversal slices were recorded with an image size of 64 × 64 pixels.

description.value: Anatomical high-resolution T1-weighted images were acquired for coregistration and normalization into standardized stereotactic space.
Data from each session were pre-processed including slice-timing, realignment, normalization into a standard Montreal Neurological Institute template, and spatial smoothing.

software.value: Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM12, Wellcome Department, London, United Kingdom)

steps.value: normalization into a standard template (Montreal Neurological Institute, MNI) with a spatial resolution of 2 × 2 × 2 mm3
smoothing with an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: The Cyberball task was modeled as three separate blocks of condition (passive watching, inclusion and exclusion), with six motion parameters integrated into the design matrix. Beta-images representing the averaged, estimated magnitude of neural activation associated with each condition were computed for each participant.

estimator.value: random effects model for group analyses

model_settings.value: The model included the factors group (HC, BPD, MD) and condition (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion), first-level contrasts for the three ball-tossing conditions, scanner type as a covariate, and age as a second covariate.

One-way ANOVA and post-hoc Newman Keuls tests were computed to analyze psychometric scales. False-discovery rate correction was applied at p < 0.05 for dependent measures such as the NTS and feelings after fMRI.
Correlation analyses between differential neural activation parameter estimates from significant clusters and BSL- and RSQ-scores within BPD patients.

description.value: Participants were asked just to watch the game and the computer controlled their character.
Participants had a random ball possession in one third of tosses.
The session started with 10 throws of 30% randomized ball possession and then participants were excluded from the game for the remaining 50 throws.
